title: Tokenizer transfer research catalog
scope: Research reference for the Tokenizer Lab hub; separate from tokenizer-only intrinsic benchmarks.
local_reproduction_claim: None. Sources and upstream code links were reviewed; methods were not executed here.

evidence_labels.paper_reported: A primary source reports the result in its own stated setting. Not a local replication.
evidence_labels.implementation_available: Upstream source code exists and was inspected for availability. Not a guarantee that it runs in the Lab environment.
evidence_labels.locally_reproduced: Reserved for a pinned, executable experiment with raw results, artifact hashes, logs and evaluation evidence. All current entries are not_run.

shared_evaluation: First validate exact UTF-8 reconstruction, special-token policy and target ID order.
Record model/tokenizer revisions, tensor shapes, dtypes, seeds, corpus identities and all output artifact hashes.
Separate initialization, auxiliary training, teacher inference and LM adaptation runtime and memory.
Use held-out original text and normalize LM likelihood by original UTF-8 bytes; cross-tokenizer perplexity per token is not directly comparable.
Keep adaptation data and compute equal for controlled comparisons; report source-language retention and per-language regressions.
Token compression, vector cosine similarity and nearest-neighbor retrieval measure different properties; none alone proves better model behavior.
Run several declared seeds when making claims about learned methods; publish individual outcomes and uncertainty rather than only the best run.

embedding_safety.input: Build rows in the exact target token-ID order and preserve the source hidden width.
embedding_safety.output: For an untied LM head, initialize and evaluate output rows separately; retain the framework orientation.
embedding_safety.tied: When weights are tied, keep one shared parameter tensor and verify that saving and reloading preserves the tie.
embedding_safety.other: Update vocabulary size, special-token IDs, padding policy and any vocabulary-sized output bias. Never silently reuse a source ID.

methods.name: Exact-row copy baseline
methods.summary: Reuse an existing model row only when the target entry has the same token semantics in the same model space.
methods.what_transfers: Existing input rows, and corresponding output rows when available. Unmatched tokens need a separately declared initializer.
requirements: Source model embedding tensors and both ID maps.
A verified token-byte and boundary-semantics match; special tokens require role matching.

compute.cpu_feasibility: Yes for copying; peak memory still depends on matrix size.
compute.training_required: No optimization for the copy itself; adaptation is a separate experiment.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: Use rows from the same checkpoint or a verified compatible model space. Equal dimensions across unrelated models are insufficient.
The same displayed text can encode different leading-space or continuation semantics. Byte overlap is a candidate match, not proof of interchangeability.

embedding_handling.other: Update vocabulary size, special-token IDs, padding policy and any vocabulary-sized output bias. Never silently reuse a source ID.

implementations.title: FOCUS
implementations.verification: primary repository inspected; not installed or executed
implementations.notes: Contains overlap copying; not a standalone Lab implementation.

evaluation_guidance: Report copied, unmatched, ambiguous and special-token counts.
Require exact equality for copied rows before and after save/load.
Compare to random and subtoken-mean initialization on the same unmatched rows.
methods.worked_example: If 800 of 1,000 target entries match, copy 800 rows; explicitly initialize the other 200. Copying is not a 100% vocabulary conversion.

methods.name: Subtoken averaging / Fast Vocabulary Transfer
methods.summary: Tokenize each target piece with the source tokenizer and average the corresponding source model rows.
methods.what_transfers: An embedding initialization built from source subpieces; it does not transfer token order or a complete model behavior.
requirements: Source tokenizer, target tokenizer and source embedding tensors.
A declared conversion from target piece bytes to valid source-tokenizer input.

compute.cpu_feasibility: Yes for initialization if the matrices fit memory.
compute.training_required: No training for the arithmetic mean; the paper evaluates additional adaptation training.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: The output width stays equal to the source model hidden width.
Handle byte fragments, leading-space markers, unknown tokens and added-token matching explicitly; arbitrary vocabulary strings are not always standalone text.

methods.worked_example: A target piece decomposed into 3 source IDs receives (e1 + e2 + e3) / 3. Each occurrence contributes one third; changing their order leaves this average unchanged.

methods.name: WECHSEL
methods.summary: Use aligned bilingual static embeddings to select source subword neighbors and combine their model rows.
methods.what_transfers: New vocabulary rows in the existing model space while retaining the model backbone.
requirements: Source and target tokenizers and source model rows.
Static embeddings covering both languages plus an alignment/dictionary policy.

compute.cpu_feasibility: Initialization is CPU-feasible; auxiliary embeddings may occupy substantial RAM.
compute.training_required: No LM training in row construction; the published adaptation results include model training.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: Bilingual-resource quality and language coverage limit the method.
Keep the source backbone and hidden width; this is not an arbitrary model-to-model vector swap.

methods.worked_example: If a new piece uses neighbor weights 0.6, 0.3 and 0.1, its row is 0.6e1 + 0.3e2 + 0.1e3. These are illustrative weights, not a measured result.

methods.name: FOCUS
methods.summary: Use shared vocabulary as anchors; choose sparse semantic combinations in an auxiliary target-token embedding space.
methods.what_transfers: Copied shared rows and weighted combinations of source model anchor rows for new entries.
requirements: Both tokenizers, source model rows and usable overlap.
Target-language text for auxiliary token embeddings, or a declared supported pretrained auxiliary resource.

compute.cpu_feasibility: CPU-feasible for auxiliary embeddings and initialization; report memory and elapsed time.
compute.training_required: Auxiliary embedding training may be needed; continued LM training is separate.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: Overlap quality matters, including special-token and boundary handling.
The reference evaluation centers on XLM-R; a decoder-model port requires its own evidence.

methods.worked_example: With 10,000 valid shared anchors, a new piece can receive a weighted combination of only a few anchor rows; publish which rows and their exact weights.

methods.name: Constrained Word2Vec (CW2V)
methods.summary: Learn new rows from target-language contexts as convex combinations of existing rows.
methods.what_transfers: Added input and LM-head rows while retaining the existing model parameters.
requirements: Expanded target tokenizer, source model rows and target-language text.
The constrained skip-gram training configuration and a held-out evaluation split.

compute.cpu_feasibility: Small prototypes can run on CPU; full matrix and corpus costs must be measured.
compute.training_required: Yes: contextual initialization training, followed by adaptation for the paper evaluations.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: The paper addresses vocabulary expansion rather than unrestricted model replacement.
Do not generalize the paper’s convex-hull guarantee beyond its stated assumptions or to arbitrary biased output heads.

embedding_handling.input: Build rows in the exact target token-ID order and preserve the source hidden width.
embedding_handling.output: The paper explicitly learns separate constrained combinations for untied input and LM-head matrices.
embedding_handling.tied: When weights are tied, keep one shared parameter tensor and verify that saving and reloading preserves the tie.
embedding_handling.other: Update vocabulary size, special-token IDs, padding policy and any vocabulary-sized output bias. Never silently reuse a source ID.

Separate initializer training time from subsequent LM adaptation.

methods.worked_example: Weights 0.5, 0.3 and 0.2 sum to 1 and keep the new row inside the existing rows’ convex hull. Their values are learned from context.

methods.name: Embedding-space mapping
methods.summary: Fit a transformation using paired anchor vectors, then project other vectors into a target model space.
methods.what_transfers: Vector coordinates; no automatic transfer of attention weights, token boundaries or generation behavior.
requirements: Source and target vector matrices plus defensible paired anchors.
Separate fitting, development and evaluation anchors with no token-family leakage.

compute.cpu_feasibility: Linear least squares or SVD is CPU-feasible at modest sizes.
compute.training_required: Yes: fitting a mapper; subsequent LM adaptation is a separate requirement to evaluate.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: Equal width permits a square orthogonal mapping; differing widths require a rectangular or other declared mapper.
MUSE is a word-embedding alignment reference, not evidence that any two LLM embedding spaces are interchangeable.
Train and evaluate input and output mappings separately if their spaces differ.

embedding_handling.input: Document source/target dimensions, centering, normalization, objective and regularization.
embedding_handling.output: Fit a separate output mapper for an untied head; do not assume the input mapper is correct for output rows.
embedding_handling.tied: When weights are tied, keep one shared parameter tensor and verify that saving and reloading preserves the tie.
embedding_handling.other: Update vocabulary size, special-token IDs, padding policy and any vocabulary-sized output bias. Never silently reuse a source ID.

methods.worked_example: For 768-dimensional source vectors and 1,024-dimensional target vectors, a linear matrix has 768 × 1,024 = 786,432 coefficients, plus 1,024 if a bias is used.

methods.name: Zero-Shot Tokenizer Transfer (ZeTT)
methods.summary: A previously trained hypernetwork predicts model-compatible rows for a new tokenizer.
methods.what_transfers: Predicted vocabulary-dependent parameters for a compatible base model and supported tokenizer representation.
requirements: A hypernetwork trained for the source model or a demonstrated compatible variant.
Source model, target tokenizer, conversion metadata and the exact hypernetwork checkpoint.

compute.cpu_feasibility: Inference may be CPU-feasible if all required tensors fit; full-scale training normally needs accelerators.
compute.training_required: Hypernetwork training is required unless using a compatible released checkpoint; zero-shot applies at transfer time.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: A hypernetwork trained for one base model is not a universal mapper for unrelated checkpoints.
The original repository describes transfer to fine-tuned variants; follow its combination rule rather than blindly reusing rows.

embedding_handling.input: Build rows in the exact target token-ID order and preserve the source hidden width.
embedding_handling.output: Require a checkpoint/configuration that predicts every required vocabulary-dependent tensor, including an untied LM head.
embedding_handling.tied: When weights are tied, keep one shared parameter tensor and verify that saving and reloading preserves the tie.
embedding_handling.other: Update vocabulary size, special-token IDs, padding policy and any vocabulary-sized output bias. Never silently reuse a source ID.

methods.name: Universal Logit Distillation (ULD)
methods.summary: Train a student using target-token supervision and a loss comparing teacher/student sorted probability masses.
methods.what_transfers: Teacher behavior through student optimization; no direct embedding-row correspondence is required.
requirements: Teacher logits, student model, both tokenizers and distillation text.
Declared prompt templates, sequence alignment/truncation and supervised-loss weights.

compute.cpu_feasibility: Toy experiments can run on CPU; useful model-scale runs usually need accelerator inference and training.
compute.training_required: Yes: teacher inference and student training.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: Teacher and student hidden widths need not match for the logit loss.
The original loss pairs positions up to the shorter sequence; positions can cover different text spans.
Sorted probability matching does not establish semantic token-to-token matches.

embedding_handling.input: The student keeps its own input parameters unless an independent initializer is used.
embedding_handling.output: Each model emits probabilities in its own vocabulary; logit caching must retain model revision, precision, temperature and masking.
embedding_handling.tied: Preserve the student’s declared tying policy; the distillation loss does not determine it.
embedding_handling.other: Update vocabulary size, special-token IDs, padding policy and any vocabulary-sized output bias. Never silently reuse a source ID.

paper_reported.scope: Treat ULD and later span-aligned or hybrid variants as separate named configurations.

implementations.title: Official ULD recipes
implementations.verification: primary repository inspected; not installed or executed
implementations.notes: Record a commit and inspect the model-specific data/prompt pipeline before reproduction.

evaluation_guidance: Publish teacher inference compute and student training compute separately.
Include a student trained on the same teacher-generated text without the ULD term.
Report aligned/omitted text, sequence-length mismatch, task metrics and held-out per-byte likelihood.
methods.worked_example: Teacher probabilities [0.6, 0.3, 0.1] and student probabilities [0.1, 0.6, 0.3] become identical after sorting. The loss alone does not know which token means what.

methods.name: Approximate Likelihood Matching (ALM)
methods.summary: Match teacher and student likelihoods of aligned text chunks, allowing different token boundaries.
methods.what_transfers: Teacher behavior through chunk-level distillation; optional components handle tokenization bias and hidden states.
requirements: Teacher and student models, tokenizer byte adapters and shared raw text.
Declared chunk alignment, divergence, loss weights and any debiasing configuration.

compute.cpu_feasibility: CPU is useful for alignment diagnostics; model-scale teacher inference and student training typically need accelerators.
compute.training_required: Yes: teacher inference and student optimization.
compute.cost_measurement: No local runtime, memory, accelerator-hours or cost measurement is available.

compatibility: Both tokenizations must represent comparable underlying bytes; expose lossy normalization and unknown-token cases.
The likelihood objective does not require equal hidden widths; optional hidden-state loss needs compatible dimensions or a declared projection.

embedding_handling.input: The student can use an independent initializer; record that initializer to isolate ALM.
embedding_handling.output: Use each model’s own output head, summing log probabilities over each aligned chunk.
embedding_handling.tied: Keep each model’s tying policy; different vocabulary sizes do not imply shared parameter rows.
embedding_handling.other: Update vocabulary size, special-token IDs, padding policy and any vocabulary-sized output bias. Never silently reuse a source ID.
